svg.text: BCBC 2024 · DIVISION B · PART 9 HOUSING AND SMALL BUILDINGS · SECTION 9.10 FIRE PROTECTION
Piping Penetrations

g.text: DWV or central vacuum pipe, not in a
Water closet drain through a concrete

Combustible DWV piping on one side of
a vertical fire separation, not in a
Combustible water piping, not in a

svg.text: WHAT THE CODE REQUIRES
Piping for drain, waste, vent and central vacuum systems not
located in a vertical shaft is permitted to penetrate a fire
separation required to have a fire-resistance rating, or a
membrane forming part of such an assembly
Provided the penetration is protected in accordance with Clause
9.10.9.6.(1)(a) or (b). Except as provided in Sentences (2) and
(5). See Note A-3.1.9.
Drain piping leading directly from a water closet through a
concrete floor slab is permitted to penetrate a horizontal
fire separation, or a membrane that contributes to its
rating, provided
(a) the piping is noncombustible and the penetration is
protected in accordance with Sentence 9.10.9.6.(1), or (b) the
piping is combustible and the penetration is sealed by a
firestop conforming to Clause 9.10.9.6.(1)(a).
Combustible drain, waste and vent piping is permitted on one
side of a vertical fire separation, provided it is not
located in a vertical shaft
In buildings containing two dwelling units only, combustible
drain, waste and vent piping is permitted on one side of a
horizontal fire separation
Water distribution piping is permitted to partly or wholly
penetrate a fire separation required to have a
fire-resistance rating, provided
(a) the piping is noncombustible and the penetration is
protected in accordance with Sentence 9.10.9.6.(1), or (b) the
piping is combustible, is not located in a vertical shaft, and
the penetration is sealed by a firestop conforming to Clause
Drawn: four samples, cut to show the framing. Orange: firestop. Pipe sizes are illustration only.
Source: BCBC 2024, Division B, Article 9.10.9.7. (page 9-68)
